headline: Canyon Permits and Cave Tour Reservations
reservation: Timpanogos Cave National Monument requires advanced reservations for guided tours, which often sell out weeks in advance. While general canyon entry is open, specific campgrounds and high-traffic areas may implement seasonal fee or access systems via Recreation.gov.

days.title: Granite Canyons and Alpine Lakes
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from Salt Lake City

stops.name: Silver Lake Boardwalk
stops.detail: Stroll an accessible path in Big Cottonwood Canyon often frequented by moose.

stops.name: Donut Falls
stops.detail: Hike to a unique waterfall where the creek plunges through a natural roof in the rock.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for transit; canyon roads are steep and winding.
days.note: Parking at popular trailheads in Big Cottonwood often fills by early morning on weekends.

days.title: Peak Summits and Olympic Echoes

stops.name: Snowbird Aerial Tram
stops.detail: Ascend to the 11,000-foot summit of Hidden Peak for views of the Salt Lake Valley.

stops.name: Utah Olympic Park
stops.detail: Visit the Olympic winter-sports venue to see the ski jumps and bobsled track.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for transit; Guardsman Pass is a seasonal route.
days.note: Check the status of Guardsman Pass before travel; it is typically closed from late autumn to early summer.

days.title: The Alpine Loop and Underground Wonders

stops.name: Timpanogos Cave National Monument
stops.detail: Hike the steep paved trail to explore three highly decorated natural caves.

stops.name: Bridal Veil Falls
stops.detail: View the massive multi-tiered waterfall located directly off the Provo Canyon road.

days.driving: Allow 2.5 hours for the full Alpine Loop; transit is slow due to narrow turns.
days.note: Cave tours are physically demanding; verify visitor health requirements on the NPS site.

intel.title: Canyon Carpooling
intel.text: Little and Big Cottonwood Canyons have limited parking at trailheads. Consider using the UTA canyon bus service during winter and peak summer periods.

intel.title: Mountain Shadows
intel.text: Cell service is generally reliable at resort bases but drops off in deep canyon narrows and high basins. Download maps for offline use before leaving the valley.

intel.title: Valley Fill-ups
intel.text: There are no gas stations within the Cottonwood Canyons or on the Alpine Loop. Refuel in Salt Lake City, Sandy, or Provo before beginning the ascent.

intel.title: Wildflower Peaks
intel.text: Albion Basin wildflowers typically peak in late July, though this varies by snowpack levels. This area may implement traffic metering during the bloom.

intel.title: Watershed Restrictions
intel.text: Big and Little Cottonwood Canyons are protected watersheds. Domestic animals and swimming are strictly prohibited to protect the metropolitan water supply.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at SLC or PVU; stop in the valley for hydration supplies and mountain-ready layers before heading into the canyons.
plan.vehicle: A vehicle with AWD/4WD and snow tires is required during winter months (Traction Law); check rental agreements for mountain road use.
plan.goldenHour: Sunset from the Guardsman Pass Overlook provides a panoramic view of the fall colors or snow-capped peaks in the Heber Valley.
